body: Every Tuesday from 6 pm to 8.30 pm, the Old Fire Station on Mill Lane opens its workshop to anyone who wants to repair their own bicycle. This is not a repair shop: our volunteers will show you what to do, but you do the work yourself. Tools and a work stand are provided free of charge. Second-hand parts such as tyres, chains and brake pads are available for a small donation, and new inner tubes are sold at cost price.

You do not need to book, but on busy evenings there may be a wait of up to thirty minutes for a stand. Please bring your bike clean — we cannot work on bikes covered in mud. Children under 12 are welcome if accompanied by an adult.

Once a month, on the first Tuesday, we run a beginners' session on basic maintenance: fixing a puncture, adjusting brakes and cleaning the chain. Places are limited to ten and must be reserved by email at least two days in advance.

items.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

headings.text: Farmers welcome the return of the predator
How the lynx was driven out

paragraphs.text: For most of the twentieth century the Eurasian lynx was absent from the forests of western and central Europe. Hunted for its fur and blamed, often unfairly, for attacks on sheep, the cat had been pushed out of Germany by 1850, out of Switzerland by the early 1900s and out of France not long afterwards. Only in the remote mountains of the Carpathians and in the forests of Scandinavia did viable populations survive. To most farmers of the time the disappearance of a large predator was not a loss but a relief, and few people imagined that the animal would ever come back. Bounties were paid for dead animals in several countries, and the last lynx in the Alps was shot in the 1930s, an event that passed almost unnoticed at the time.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The first serious attempt to bring the lynx back took place in Switzerland in 1971, when a small number of animals captured in the Carpathians were released in the Alps. The project was not announced in advance, partly because the organisers feared opposition from hunters and shepherds and preferred to present them with an accomplished fact. The animals settled, bred and slowly spread along the mountain chain. Similar releases followed in the French Jura, in Slovenia and, from 2000 onwards, in the Harz mountains of Germany. Today several hundred lynx live in the Alps and the Jura, and the species is once again breeding in at least eight countries where it had been lost. The first animals were fitted with radio collars so that their movements could be followed, and within a decade the first cubs born in the wild were recorded.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The return has been possible because the forests themselves recovered. As people left the countryside for the cities, farmland on steep slopes was abandoned and trees grew back over it. Roe deer, the lynx's main prey, became far more numerous than at any time in living memory; in some regions they are now so common that foresters regard them as a pest, since they eat young trees before these can grow above the height of a deer's mouth. A predator that takes roughly one deer a week therefore looks, to a forester, like a free service. Studies in Switzerland suggest that where lynx are present, deer avoid open clearings and browse less heavily, allowing young trees to survive and the forest to renew itself. Farmers, too, have less reason to complain than they once had: in Switzerland the state now compensates them for each sheep that is proven to have been killed by a lynx, and the number of such claims is small.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Nevertheless, the lynx's future is far from secure. The reintroduced populations are small and isolated from one another by motorways, railways and farmland, so that animals from one area rarely meet those from another. Genetic studies show that the Swiss population, descended from fewer than twenty founders, has lost much of its variety, which may reduce its resistance to disease. Illegal killing continues, especially where hunters believe the cats compete with them for deer, and some shepherds still lose lambs each spring. Conservationists argue that the answer is not more releases but corridors of forest linking the existing groups, so that the lynx can find their own way between them. Whether landowners will accept a wider network of wild land remains an open question. Even so, the fact that a large predator has returned at all to some of the most crowded landscapes in Europe is, for many biologists, a reason for cautious optimism.
paragraphs.label: D

items.prompt: Monthly fee: £ ____

explanation.en: She first says "twelve pounds" but corrects herself: "sorry, no… it's fifteen pounds now". The corrected figure counts.
explanation.kk: Алдымен «twelve pounds» айтылады, бірақ сөйлеуші өзін түзетеді: «sorry, no… it's fifteen pounds now». Түзетілген сан есептеледі.
explanation.ru: Сначала звучит «twelve pounds», но говорящая поправляет себя: «sorry, no… it's fifteen pounds now». Засчитывается исправленная цифра.

items.quote: there's a code for the gate. It's 4-7-1-9.
items.prompt: Gate code: ____

explanation.en: The code is read digit by digit: "4-7-1-9". Write the digits one at a time rather than trying to hold the whole number in memory.
explanation.kk: Кодты цифрамен оқиды: «4-7-1-9». Цифрларды бір-бірлеп жазыңыз, санды тұтас есте сақтауға тырыспаңыз.
explanation.ru: Код диктуют по цифрам: «4-7-1-9». Записывайте цифры по одной, не пытайтесь запомнить число целиком.

clips.context: A man phones a community garden about renting a plot.
clips.transcript:
SANDRA: Greenway Community Garden, Sandra speaking.
TOM: Oh, hello. I'm ringing about renting a plot. Is there anything free at the moment?
SANDRA: There is, actually — one of the small plots came free last week. It's four metres by three, so twelve square metres.
TOM: That sounds ideal. And what does it cost?
SANDRA: The small plots are twelve pounds a month... sorry, no, that was last year. It went up in April, so it's fifteen pounds now. That includes water and use of the shared tools.
TOM: Fifteen. Fine. Are there any rules I should know about?
SANDRA: The main one is no bonfires — we had complaints from the neighbours. And we ask everyone to come to at least one work party a season. The next one is on Saturday the twenty-first.
TOM: Saturday the twenty-first. I'll put that in my diary. How do I get in? Is there a key?
SANDRA: No, there's a code for the gate. It's 4-7-1-9. Don't share it, please.
TOM: 4-7-1-9. Got it. And who do I ask if I need a hand?
SANDRA: That's Marcus — he's the site manager, he's usually there in the mornings.
clips.instruction: Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

items.quote: On weekdays the pool will open at seven in the morning instead of eight
items.prompt: New weekday opening time: ____ am

explanation.en: "…will open at seven in the morning instead of eight": the new time is 7; "eight" is the old time, a distractor.
explanation.kk: «…will open at seven in the morning instead of eight»: жаңа уақыт — 7. «Eight» — ескі уақыт, жаңылыстыратын сан.
explanation.ru: «…will open at seven in the morning instead of eight»: новое время — 7, «eight» — старое, это отвлекающая цифра.

items.quote: the small pool will be closed all next week for cleaning
items.prompt: The ____ pool is closed next week

explanation.en: "The small pool" is closed; the "main pool" is only mentioned as where the lessons move to.
explanation.kk: «The small pool» жабылады; «main pool» сабақтар ауысатын орын ретінде айтылады — шатастырмаңыз.
explanation.ru: Закрыт «the small pool»; «main pool» упоминается как место, куда переносят занятия — не путайте.

items.quote: free tea or coffee to anyone who swims before eight in the morning
items.prompt: Free tea or coffee for people who swim before ____ am

explanation.en: "…anyone who swims before eight in the morning". Here "eight" is the answer, even though the same number was a distractor in question 1.
explanation.kk: «…anyone who swims before eight in the morning». Мұнда «eight» — дұрыс жауап; 1-сұрақта дәл осы сан жаңылыстыратын сан болған.
explanation.ru: «…anyone who swims before eight in the morning». Здесь «eight» — верный ответ, хотя в вопросе 1 та же цифра была ловушкой.

clips.context: An announcement at a leisure centre about new opening hours.
clips.transcript: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Lakeside Leisure Centre. Just a quick announcement before the pool opens. From next Monday, our opening hours are changing. On weekdays the pool will open at seven in the morning instead of eight, so early swimmers can come before work. Closing time stays the same at nine in the evening. At weekends we'll open at nine and close at five. Please note that the small pool will be closed all next week for cleaning, so lessons for children will take place in the main pool. Lockers now need a one-pound coin, which you get back. Finally, the café is offering free tea or coffee to anyone who swims before eight in the morning during the first week. Enjoy your swim.
clips.instruction: Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

items.quote: city gardens have flowers almost all year, whereas farmland has one crop that flowers for a few weeks
items.prompt: According to the council report, city bees do better than country bees because

options.text: there is less pollution in cities than people expect.
city gardens provide food for most of the year.
there are fewer diseases in cities.

explanation.en: Dan explains: "city gardens have flowers almost all year". Pollution is only Priya's wrong assumption (A); diseases are never mentioned (C).
explanation.kk: Дэн түсіндіреді: «city gardens have flowers almost all year». Ластану туралы тек Прия айтады, әрі бұл оның қате жорамалы (A). Аурулар туралы сөз жоқ (C).
explanation.ru: Дэн объясняет: «city gardens have flowers almost all year». Про загрязнение говорит только Прия, и это её ошибочное предположение (A). О болезнях речи нет (C).

items.quote: What about the shortage of nesting sites? … OK, nesting sites it is.
items.prompt: Which problem do the students agree to focus on?

options.text: the lack of places to nest

explanation.en: Priya first suggests pesticides (A), but Dan persuades her and she agrees: "OK, nesting sites it is". "Shortage of nesting sites" = "lack of places to nest".
explanation.kk: Прия алдымен пестицидтерді ұсынады (A), бірақ Дэн көндіреді, ол келіседі: «OK, nesting sites it is». «Shortage of nesting sites» = «lack of places to nest».
explanation.ru: Прия сначала предлагает пестициды (A), но Дэн убеждает её, и она соглашается: «OK, nesting sites it is». «Shortage of nesting sites» = «lack of places to nest».

items.quote: Fine — Friday for slides, Monday to rehearse.
items.prompt: What will the students do on Monday?

explanation.en: The plan changes twice. The final version: "Friday for slides, Monday to rehearse". "Rehearse" = "practise". Photos are on Sunday.
explanation.kk: Жоспар екі рет өзгереді. Қорытынды: «Friday for slides, Monday to rehearse». «Rehearse» = «practise». Фото — жексенбіде.
explanation.ru: План меняется дважды. Итог: «Friday for slides, Monday to rehearse». «Rehearse» = «practise». Фото — в воскресенье.

clips.context: Two students plan a presentation on bees in cities.
clips.transcript:
PRIYA: So, Dan, for the presentation on urban bees — did you get hold of that council report?
DAN: I did. It's more interesting than I expected. The main point is that bees in the city are actually doing better than bees in the countryside.
PRIYA: Really? I assumed it would be the other way round, with all the pollution.
DAN: That's what most people think. But the report says city gardens have flowers almost all year, whereas farmland has one crop that flowers for a few weeks and then nothing.
PRIYA: So it's the variety of food, not the amount.
DAN: Exactly. Now, the tutor said we should focus on one problem rather than trying to cover everything.
PRIYA: I thought we'd do pesticides — that's the obvious one.
DAN: I'd rather not. Everyone will choose that. What about the shortage of nesting sites? Hardly anyone talks about it, and there's good data in the report.
PRIYA: Hmm. I'm not sure the audience will find it as dramatic, but you're right that it'll stand out. OK, nesting sites it is.
DAN: Great. For the visuals, I was going to use photos from the council website.
PRIYA: We can't — they're copyrighted. I'll take some myself at the allotments on Sunday. My cousin keeps a hive there.
DAN: Perfect. And I'll draft the slides by Thursday so we can rehearse on Friday.
PRIYA: Thursday's tight for me. Can we say Friday for the slides and rehearse on Monday?
DAN: Fine — Friday for slides, Monday to rehearse.
clips.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

items.quote: It's a rucksack — a blue one, quite small, with a black zip.
items.prompt: Lost item: a blue ____

explanation.en: "It's a rucksack — a blue one". You need the word from the recording; "bag" or "backpack" are not accepted. Watch the spelling: rucksack.
explanation.kk: «It's a rucksack — a blue one». Аудиодағы сөз керек: «bag» немесе «backpack» есептелмейді. Емлесіне назар аударыңыз: rucksack.
explanation.ru: «It's a rucksack — a blue one». Нужно именно слово из аудио: «bag» или «backpack» не засчитываются. Следите за написанием: rucksack.

items.quote: There's a keyring on the strap shaped like a fish.
items.prompt: Keyring shaped like a ____

explanation.en: "…a keyring on the strap shaped like a fish". The other objects (laptop, notebook, glasses) are the contents, not the keyring.
explanation.kk: «…a keyring on the strap shaped like a fish». Басқа заттар (laptop, notebook, glasses) — сөмкенің ішіндегілер, брелок емес.
explanation.ru: «…a keyring on the strap shaped like a fish». Другие предметы (laptop, notebook, glasses) — содержимое сумки, не брелок.

items.quote: It's Lena Kowalski. That's K-O-W-A-L-S-K-I.
items.prompt: Surname: ____

explanation.en: The surname is spelled out: K-O-W-A-L-S-K-I. One wrong letter means the answer is not accepted.
explanation.kk: Тегін әріптеп айтады: K-O-W-A-L-S-K-I. Бір әріптегі қате = жауап есептелмейді.
explanation.ru: Фамилию диктуют по буквам: K-O-W-A-L-S-K-I. Ошибка в одной букве = ответ не засчитан.

items.quote: You can collect it from the office at platform three. We're open until seven tonight.
items.prompt: Collect from the office at platform ____

explanation.en: "…the office at platform three". "Seven" is the closing time, not the platform.
explanation.kk: «…the office at platform three». «Seven» саны — жабылу уақыты, платформа емес.
explanation.ru: «…the office at platform three». Цифра «seven» — время закрытия, не платформа.

clips.context: A woman phones a station lost property office about a bag.
clips.transcript:
OFFICER: Station lost property, how can I help?
LENA: Hi, I think I left a bag on the train this morning. The 8.15 from Ashford.
OFFICER: OK. Can you describe it for me?
LENA: It's a rucksack — a blue one, quite small, with a black zip. There's a keyring on the strap shaped like a fish.
OFFICER: A blue rucksack with a fish keyring. Anything inside?
LENA: My laptop, unfortunately, and a green notebook. Oh, and a pair of glasses.
OFFICER: I'll check. … Yes — we've got a blue rucksack that came in about half an hour ago. Can I take your name?
LENA: It's Lena Kowalski. That's K-O-W-A-L-S-K-I.
OFFICER: And a phone number?
LENA: 0-7-7-0-0, 9-0-0-4-6-2.
OFFICER: Thanks. You can collect it from the office at platform three. We're open until seven tonight.
LENA: Platform three, until seven. Brilliant, thank you.
clips.instruction: Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

items.quote: The tower has one hundred and thirty-two steps — not one hundred and twenty-three, as it says in the old leaflet
items.prompt: Number of steps in the tower: ____

explanation.en: The guide says "one hundred and thirty-two steps — not one hundred and twenty-three". The first number is correct; the second is what the old leaflet says.
explanation.kk: Гид «one hundred and thirty-two steps — not one hundred and twenty-three» дейді. Бірінші сан дұрыс; екіншісі — ескі буклеттегі сан.
explanation.ru: Гид говорит «one hundred and thirty-two steps — not one hundred and twenty-three». Верна первая цифра; вторая — то, что написано в старом буклете.

items.quote: then we'll climb to the lamp room, and finish on the balcony, weather permitting.
items.prompt: The tour finishes on the ____

explanation.en: The order is cottage → lamp room → balcony. "Finish" sits right next to "balcony".
explanation.kk: Реті: cottage → lamp room → balcony. «Finish» сөзі «balcony» сөзінің жанында айтылады.
explanation.ru: Порядок: cottage → lamp room → balcony. Слово «finish» стоит рядом с «balcony».

items.quote: Photography is welcome everywhere except in the lamp room, because the flash damages the old lens.
items.prompt: Where is photography NOT allowed?

explanation.en: "Photography is welcome everywhere except in the lamp room". "Except" reverses the meaning: allowed everywhere but there.
explanation.kk: «Photography is welcome everywhere except in the lamp room». «Except» сөзі мағынаны өзгертеді: барлық жерде рұқсат, тек одан басқа.
explanation.ru: «Photography is welcome everywhere except in the lamp room». Слово «except» переворачивает смысл: разрешено везде, кроме.

items.quote: the gift shop sells a booklet about the lighthouse for four pounds
items.prompt: Price of the booklet: £ ____

explanation.en: "…a booklet about the lighthouse for four pounds". Don't confuse it with "forty-five minutes", the length of the tour.
explanation.kk: «…a booklet about the lighthouse for four pounds». «Forty-five minutes» дегенмен шатастырмаңыз — ол турдың ұзақтығы.
explanation.ru: «…a booklet about the lighthouse for four pounds». Не путайте с «forty-five minutes» — это длительность тура.

clips.context: A guide introduces a tour of a lighthouse.
clips.transcript: Welcome to the Point Harrow Lighthouse. My name's Rowan and I'll be your guide this afternoon. Before we go up, a few practical things. The tower has one hundred and thirty-two steps — not one hundred and twenty-three, as it says in the old leaflet — so take your time. The tour lasts about forty-five minutes. We'll start in the keeper's cottage, where you can see the original logbooks; then we'll climb to the lamp room, and finish on the balcony, weather permitting. Photography is welcome everywhere except in the lamp room, because the flash damages the old lens. If you have young children, please keep hold of their hands on the balcony — the railing is quite low. Toilets are in the visitor centre, not in the tower, so go now if you need to. Lastly, the gift shop sells a booklet about the lighthouse for four pounds, and all the money goes to the restoration fund. Right, follow me.
clips.instruction: Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. For question 3, choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

items.quote: Young zebra finches learn their song by copying an adult, usually their father.
items.prompt: Young zebra finches usually copy the song of their ____.

explanation.en: "…by copying an adult, usually their father". The sentence already has "their", so one word is needed — father; "adult" is too general.
explanation.kk: «…by copying an adult, usually their father». Сөйлемде «their» бар, сондықтан бір сөз керек — father; «adult» тым жалпы.
explanation.ru: «…by copying an adult, usually their father». В предложении уже есть «their», значит нужно одно слово — father; «adult» слишком общо.

items.quote: In the morning, straight after sleep, the young birds' songs were actually worse — less accurate — than they had been the previous evening.
items.prompt: What surprised the researchers about the birds' morning songs?

options.text: They were longer than the evening before.
They were less accurate than the evening before.

explanation.en: "…songs were actually worse — less accurate — than … the previous evening". Option B repeats the lecturer's wording; length and a different adult are never mentioned.
explanation.kk: «…songs were actually worse — less accurate — than … the previous evening». B жауабы дәрістегі сөзді қайталайды; ұзындық пен басқа ересек туралы айтылмайды.
explanation.ru: «…songs were actually worse — less accurate — than … the previous evening». Ответ B повторяет формулировку лекции; про длину и другого взрослого не говорится.

items.quote: The birds that showed the biggest drop in the morning ended up with the most accurate adult song.
items.prompt: The birds with the biggest overnight drop in quality

options.text: produced the most accurate adult song.

explanation.en: The trap is "worse = bad"; the lecturer says the opposite — "the biggest drop … ended up with the most accurate adult song".
explanation.kk: «Нашарлау деген — жаман» деп ойлау — тұзақ: лектор керісінше айтады — «the biggest drop … ended up with the most accurate adult song».
explanation.ru: Ловушка «ухудшение = плохо»: лектор говорит обратное — «the biggest drop … ended up with the most accurate adult song».

items.quote: a session shortly before sleep may be worth more than the same session in the morning.
items.prompt: The speaker suggests that practising shortly before ____ may be more effective.

explanation.en: "…a session shortly before sleep may be worth more". "Worth more" is paraphrased as "more effective".
explanation.kk: «…a session shortly before sleep may be worth more». «Worth more» → «more effective» деп өзгертілген.
explanation.ru: «…a session shortly before sleep may be worth more». «Worth more» перефразировано как «more effective».

clips.context: Part of a lecture on sleep and memory in songbirds.
clips.transcript: Today I want to look at what sleep does for memory, and I'll use a rather unexpected example: songbirds. Young zebra finches learn their song by copying an adult, usually their father. For a long time, researchers assumed that the learning happened during the day, while the young bird was listening and practising. What the recordings showed, however, was surprising. In the morning, straight after sleep, the young birds' songs were actually worse — less accurate — than they had been the previous evening. By the end of the day the song had improved again, and overall it was better than the day before. So the overnight deterioration wasn't a failure; it seemed to be part of the process. The birds that showed the biggest drop in the morning ended up with the most accurate adult song. One explanation is that during sleep the brain replays the day's practice and reorganises it, temporarily disrupting performance while making the memory more stable. A similar pattern has since been found in people learning a new motor skill, such as a sequence on a keyboard. What this suggests is that the timing of practice matters: a session shortly before sleep may be worth more than the same session in the morning.
clips.instruction: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer. For questions 2 and 3, choose the correct letter, A, B or C.
